questions.statement: Which words are parts of a computer?
questions.context: In the computer room in Medellín, students see a screen, a keyboard and a mouse on each desk.

options.feedback: Pencil, notebook and eraser are school supplies, not computer parts.
Apple, banana and orange are fruits, not computer parts.
Screen, keyboard and mouse are basic parts of a computer.
Shirt, pants and shoes are clothes, not computer parts.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta introduce vocabulario esencial de tecnología en inglés. También ayuda a reconocer los objetos de la sala de informática escolar.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Bogotá, a teacher says: "Click on the red button to open the game."

options.feedback: Writing with the keyboard is called "type", not "click".
Speaking into the microphone is called "talk", not "click".
Turning off the screen is called "turn off", not "click".
To click means to press a button on the mouse.

questions.explanation: El verbo click describe la acción principal con el ratón. También es fundamental para seguir instrucciones básicas en inglés en el computador.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In the school library in Cali, a girl wants to find information about whales on the internet.

options.feedback: To search means to look for information on the internet.
The calculator does not search for information about animals.
The trash bin deletes files and does not search the internet.
Turning off the computer stops the activity and finds nothing.

questions.explanation: El verbo search se usa para buscar información en internet. También se practica la secuencia correcta para investigar temas escolares en línea.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the correct order of safe actions?
questions.context: In Cartagena, students read a poster: "Type your name. Click Save. Do not share your password."

options.text: Share your password, then click Save.
options.feedback: Sharing your password is dangerous and not safe.

options.text: Click Save, type your name, share your password.
options.feedback: This order is wrong and sharing passwords is unsafe.

options.text: Type your name, click Save, keep your password secret.
options.feedback: This order follows the poster and keeps the password secret.

options.text: Share your password with friends in the chat.
options.feedback: Sharing passwords in chats is never safe on the internet.

questions.explanation: Seguir instrucciones en orden es clave en la sala de informática. También se refuerza la regla de nunca compartir contraseñas en internet.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence.
questions.context: In Bucaramanga, a boy writes a story: "I _____ my homework on the computer every afternoon."

options.feedback: "Click" is for the mouse, not for writing homework.
"Type" means to write with the keyboard on the computer.
"Search" means to look for information, not to write homework.
"Print" means to put paper work out, not to write it.

questions.explanation: El verbo type significa escribir con el teclado del computador. También se diferencia de otros verbos tecnológicos como click y search.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Pereira, a girl receives a message from a stranger: "Hello, send me your photo and your address."

options.text: Send the photo and the address quickly.
options.feedback: Sending personal information to strangers is very dangerous.

options.text: Do not answer and tell a teacher or parent.
options.feedback: Telling a trusted adult is the safest action with strangers.
Sharing passwords puts the whole school at risk.

options.text: Meet the stranger alone after school.
options.feedback: Meeting strangers alone is never safe for children.

questions.explanation: La seguridad en internet exige no compartir datos personales. También es vital avisar a un adulto de confianza ante mensajes extraños.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which rule is better for a fifth grader?
questions.context: In Santa Marta, students compare two rules: "Play two hours online every day" and "Ask permission and play thirty minutes after homework."

options.text: Ask permission and play thirty minutes after homework.
options.feedback: This rule balances study, rest and short safe screen time.

options.text: Play two hours online every day alone.
options.feedback: Long hours alone online are unhealthy and unsafe.

options.text: Use the computer all night without permission.
options.feedback: Using the computer all night harms health and breaks rules.

options.text: Never do homework and only play games.
options.feedback: Homework is important and games should not replace study.

questions.explanation: Analizar hábitos digitales ayuda a usar la tecnología con equilibrio. También se promueve pedir permiso y priorizar las tareas escolares primero.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which set of instructions is the clearest and most correct?
questions.context: In Manizales, a class writes instructions: "First, turn on the computer. Then, open the browser. Finally, search for homework help."

options.text: Computer on. Browser thing. Search maybe.
options.feedback: These words are incomplete and the order is unclear.

options.text: Turn off, never open, never search.
options.feedback: These steps stop the task instead of helping with homework.

options.text: First turn on the computer, then open the browser, finally search for help.
options.feedback: This set uses clear verbs, correct order and polite sequence words.

options.text: Search first, turn on later, open never.
options.feedback: This order is impossible because the computer is still off.

questions.explanation: Evaluar instrucciones exige revisar orden, verbos y claridad. También se practican conectores como first, then y finally para guías tecnológicas.
questions.subject: ingles
